1.content:
A resting limit order can supply liquidity; a marketable order takes available liquidity. Maker–taker venues can rebate posted liquidity, while inverted venues charge for posting. Fees depend on the venue, product, participant and tier. Check the actual schedule rather than assuming every maker is paid.

Quotes can be added, cancelled or repriced. A fast chart move does not establish which firm withdrew quotes or prove that a three-candle FVG contains no executed trades.
1.keyTakeaway: A resting limit order can supply liquidity; a marketable order takes available liquidity.

2.content:
Cumulative Volume Delta (CVD) accumulates a feed’s classification of buyer-initiated minus seller-initiated executed volume. Price and delta may diverge. Repeated selling without a lower traded price can motivate an absorption hypothesis, but does not identify an institution or guarantee a reversal.

Record the feed, classification method, reset time and instrument. Spot-FX broker volume is not consolidated exchange-wide volume. Compare continuation and failed-reversal cases as well as attractive examples.
2.keyTakeaway: Cumulative Volume Delta (CVD) accumulates a feed’s classification of buyer-initiated minus seller-initiated executed volume.

keyTerms.definition: A matching convention that prioritizes price, then arrival time at that price; the product may use another allocation algorithm.
A venue fee structure that distinguishes adding from removing liquidity; rebates are not universal.
Cumulative classified buyer-initiated volume minus seller-initiated volume for a stated feed and reset interval.
An interpretation of executed flow and limited price progress; it does not establish participant identity.

summary: A resting limit order can supply liquidity; a marketable order takes available liquidity.
Cumulative Volume Delta (CVD) accumulates a feed’s classification of buyer-initiated minus seller-initiated executed volume.

0.content:
Market-data products expose different information: top-of-book prices, aggregated depth or order-level messages. Availability, latency, hidden quantity and venue coverage vary. Displayed depth is not the whole market or a record of every stop order.

A large quote can disappear through execution, cancellation or amendment. The disappearance alone does not establish spoofing intent. Compare quote messages with trades where available, and state what the feed omits.
0.keyTakeaway: Market-data products expose different information: top-of-book prices, aggregated depth or order-level messages.

1.content:
TWAP distributes execution over a stated time schedule; VWAP execution seeks a volume-weighted benchmark using a chosen participation profile. An iceberg displays only part of its total quantity under the venue’s rules. None eliminates market impact or guarantees a benchmark fill.

These are execution concepts, not candle-reading proof. An order-block rectangle cannot identify a particular execution algorithm, its remaining inventory or the participant using it.
1.keyTakeaway: TWAP distributes execution over a stated time schedule; VWAP execution seeks a volume-weighted benchmark using a chosen participation profile.

0.content:
Market liquidity concerns the ability to transact a stated quantity at available prices with associated spread and price impact. ICT’s buy-side and sell-side labels instead mark hypothesized order interest beyond selected highs and lows. Keep these two uses of liquidity distinct.

A visible high is an observable reference. The number, ownership and exact prices of stops beyond it are not visible in an OHLC candle. Select the reference before the later breach.
0.keyTakeaway: Market liquidity concerns the ability to transact a stated quantity at available prices with associated spread and price impact.

1.content:
A sweep study records a trade beyond a previously selected high or low, followed by a specified response. State whether a wick or close counts and how long a return may take. A breach can continue rather than reverse.

Triggered stop-market orders and stop-limit orders behave differently. Execution price, available quantity and slippage are not established by the sweep label. A return inside the range does not prove that every stop was filled or reveal who took the other side.
1.keyTakeaway: A sweep study records a trade beyond a previously selected high or low, followed by a specified response.

2.content:
Within a selected dealing range, an internal reference may be an FVG or another chosen price interval; external references may be the range extremes. This is a chart framework, not a closed-loop law requiring price to alternate between them.

Mark the boundaries and observation horizon in advance. Record a return, partial return, continuation and no return separately. Moving the range afterward changes the study and can hide failed hypotheses.

0.content:
A candle records the open, high, low and close over a specified interval and feed. Its body spans open to close; its wicks show the remaining extremes. These four values do not show where most volume traded, the exact intrabar path or participant identity.

Check whether the chart uses trades, bids, asks or another price series. Two feeds or session boundaries can produce different candles without either candle proving manipulation.

A wick crossing a level and a body close beyond it are different observations. Choose the rule required by the particular lesson. The reviewed 2022 Episode 3 discussion does not require a universal body-close rule for every initial structure crossing.

A wick is not automatically a false move, and a body close is not proof of genuine institutional intent. Record the initial crossing and later candle completion separately rather than deciding which one counted after seeing the outcome.
0.keyTakeaway: A candle records the open, high, low and close over a specified interval and feed.

1.content:
Displacement describes a relatively strong move under a stated measurement convention. For example, compare body size or range with a prior sample on the same instrument and timeframe. No universal candle count, wick size or volume threshold is supplied here.

A completed three-candle FVG is a separate geometric observation. Strong movement can occur without that pattern, and its presence does not identify a bank or guarantee a later retracement. Define the measure before replay.
1.keyTakeaway: Displacement describes a relatively strong move under a stated measurement convention.

2.content:
A swing’s role depends on the timeframe and selection rule. A minor break may be a local retracement or part of a wider reversal; neither label is known with certainty from the break alone. Higher-timeframe references provide context, not an infallible hierarchy.

Freeze the three-candle pivot rule, tie handling and confirmation delay. A pivot requiring a right-hand candle is not available before that candle forms. Compare how the same event appears on two timeframes without backdating the signal.
2.keyTakeaway: A swing’s role depends on the timeframe and selection rule.

0.content:
For this study, a bullish continuation BOS is a break above a selected prior swing high within an already defined upward structure; reverse the logic for bearish continuation. State whether an intrabar crossing or a completed close qualifies.

A break is an observable price event, not proof that institutions control the next move. Displacement and a completed FVG can be additional conditions in a named variation, but are not automatically present after every break.
0.keyTakeaway: For this study, a bullish continuation BOS is a break above a selected prior swing high within an already defined upward structure; reverse the logic for bearish continuation.

1.content:
A protected swing is the reference whose breach would contradict your stated structural interpretation. Weak high or weak low is a framework label for a candidate objective. Neither describes a level that cannot break or a target that must be reached.

Select the reference while it is visible, record its timestamp, and define wick-versus-close invalidation. Different swing selection can change the label; disclose that judgment rather than moving the reference after a losing example.
1.keyTakeaway: A protected swing is the reference whose breach would contradict your stated structural interpretation.

2.content:
A breakout entry and a retracement entry are distinct research variations. Waiting for a return to a completed FVG may change price, stop distance and fill frequency; the return may never occur. Neither method has a verified advantage established by this chapter.

Specify order type, expiry, invalidation and costs before replay. Keep unfilled orders and failed continuations in the sample. A close beyond structure does not make a stop safe or establish positive expectancy.

Choose the swing and wick-or-close rule in advance. The same local event may be a retracement on a wider chart. A candle chart cannot establish whether the move came from profit taking, new positions or a particular institution.

1.content:
CHoCH and MSS are used differently across trading communities and source lessons. Do not impose a universal hierarchy in which one label mathematically verifies a regime change. The separate MSS chapter records the reviewed source’s crossing and displacement conventions.

Write which event you mean: crossing a chosen swing, closing beyond it, or completing an FVG. Higher-timeframe location can be a context filter in your selected variation; it does not prove the next direction.
1.keyTakeaway: CHoCH and MSS are used differently across trading communities and source lessons.

2.content:
An earlier entry can have a different fill price and failure rate from an entry deferred until more candles complete. A smaller planned stop or larger reward-to-risk ratio does not establish a better outcome. No comparative win rate is verified here.

Keep the variants separate and apply the same transaction-cost assumptions. Save the information visible at each decision. Include false breaks and missed entries rather than comparing only completed winners.

An FVG midpoint or an order-block reference can define a research entry, but neither establishes exceptional profitability. A news waiting period is a chosen restriction, not proof that spreads or fills become safe afterward. Record costs, invalidation and unfilled orders.

2.content:
Inducement is an interpretation that a selected nearer swing could attract orders before price reaches another reference. Mark the nearer and farther references before the move; a chart does not reveal who placed orders or deliberately trapped another trader.

Do not turn the label into a rule that the first order block must fail. Compare first reactions, later reactions, continuations and no-return examples under the same entry and expiry rules.
2.keyTakeaway: Inducement is an interpretation that a selected nearer swing could attract orders before price reaches another reference.

3.content:
SMT compares corresponding highs or lows in specified related markets over aligned times. A divergence may be visible and later disappear; correlation varies and does not establish immediate institutional intent.

Define the market condition and selected price reference before considering a trade. The midnight opening price is a time-and-price reference, while premium or discount is measured against the midpoint of a named range. They are not interchangeable definitions. Keep uncertainty visible even when several labels agree.

A 20-day lookback is a selected research window. State its anchor, trading calendar and whether the current incomplete day is excluded. Mark the high, low and candidate prior references using only data available at that point.

The midpoint partitions that chosen range into premium and discount. It is not an inventory measurement or a reason price must reverse. Rolling the window or selecting a different anchor changes the references and must be recorded.
1.keyTakeaway: A 20-day lookback is a selected research window.

2.content:
Treat an OTE retracement, an FVG return and an order-block return as separately specified entry variations unless the linked source explicitly combines them. A familiar Fibonacci percentage does not by itself authenticate the original Model 1 trade plan.

Before replay, state the reference swing, entry order and invalidation. A one- or two-tick buffer and an automatic breakeven move are not universally suitable. Product increment, spread and slippage change the execution assumptions.
2.keyTakeaway: Treat an OTE retracement, an FVG return and an order-block return as separately specified entry variations unless the linked source explicitly combines them.

3.content:
A partial exit realizes profit or loss on only the closed portion; a stop modification changes the remaining order’s exposure without realizing that amount. Keep these actions distinct when comparing the original plan and a research variation.

Fixed exit splits and pip distances are not universal evidence of positive expectancy. Record all orders, costs, missed fills and the final net outcome. Three orders sharing one idea still contribute to one combined risk budget.

2.content:

1.content:
COT is a delayed positioning report, not a live order book. In replay, distinguish the snapshot date from the later publication time and use only a release already available at the decision point. Select the report family and futures-only or combined basis explicitly.

Net positions are longs minus shorts within a category. A commercial net-long reading does not alone predict an imminent rally or represent all spot-FX participants. The related Month 10 source discusses why the net number alone is insufficient.

2.content:
A 40- or 60-trading-day lookback can supply broader references. It is not a measured central-bank inventory cycle. State the anchor and the treatment of incomplete sessions; compare premium and discount only within the named range.

Positioning context and chart location are separate inputs. Neither makes the other correct. Keep dates aligned and record instances when the proposed direction fails or a candidate entry never develops.
2.keyTakeaway: A 40- or 60-trading-day lookback can supply broader references.

3.content:
A daily reference can be refined on a four-hour chart as a named study variation. Save the actual entry condition, initial stop and expiry. A wider stop does not guarantee survival, and a narrower one may be reached before a later favorable move.

Partial-exit percentages are management choices, not universal rules. Include overnight costs, gaps, slippage and correlated positions in combined exposure. Evaluate realized outcomes rather than assuming a particular exit split creates an edge.

Pyramiding adds exposure. Recalculate combined loss under the actual stop and gap assumptions before adding a position. Existing unrealized profit is not realized cash, and scaling cannot guarantee an exponential return or prevent a drawdown.

ICT uses smart-money language as an explanatory framework for selected price patterns. A claim that one interbank algorithm controls all markets is not established by an OHLC chart or by this curriculum. Exchanges, dealers, hedgers and speculators participate under different market structures.

A large participant may use several execution methods; neither market orders nor liquidity provision belongs exclusively to one group. A candle cannot divide all traders into informed institutions and uninformed retail or show who deliberately moved a price.

1.content:
Expansion, retracement, reversal and consolidation are descriptive categories relative to a chosen scale. Expansion is a directional departure; retracement is a counter-move within the selected context; reversal changes that context; consolidation stays within selected bounds.

Choose the timeframe, boundaries and confirmation delay. The same price path may consolidate on one chart and expand on another. No category by itself establishes institutional sponsorship, an inevitable FVG or what the next candle must do.
1.keyTakeaway: Expansion, retracement, reversal and consolidation are descriptive categories relative to a chosen scale.

2.content:
Select a high and low to define a dealing range, then calculate midpoint = (high + low) / 2. Above that midpoint is premium and below it is discount relative to this range. A different range can change the classification.

Premium and discount are not measurements of fair economic value or proof of distribution and accumulation. A discount-only entry is a chosen model restriction, not a universal law forbidding all purchases above a midpoint.
2.keyTakeaway: Select a high and low to define a dealing range, then calculate midpoint = (high + low) / 2.

3.content:
A run beyond a selected high or low is observable. Calling it an intentional raid is an interpretation that requires more evidence than the completed candle. Orders can be triggered without a later reversal, and not every stop order becomes a market order.

A subsequent impulse can define a new research range if your rule specifies when the swing completes. Save the previous range and do not redraw it retroactively to remove failed examples. Timing and participant identity remain separate questions.
3.keyTakeaway: A run beyond a selected high or low is observable.

3.content:
Head-and-shoulders patterns and comparable highs or lows can supply research references. They do not require either a textbook reversal or a stop-run reversal. Define the tolerances and structural condition rather than assuming every trader sees the same pattern.

2.content:
LRLR and HRLR are framework descriptions of a proposed path with fewer or more selected opposing references. Their classification depends on the timeframe and which arrays or swings you count. A visually clear path is not frictionless execution.

Freeze the classification before the move. Compare elapsed time, adverse movement, spread and failed objectives across both groups. The labels alone establish neither the easiest profits nor a verified rule that only one group may be traded.

After a proposed weekly objective is reached, continuation, consolidation and reversal all remain possible. Do not assign a lower probability to Thursday or Friday without a defined dataset. A target touch and a completed daily entry condition are separate observations.

A London-open Judas-swing example and a London-close retracement study use different observation windows. Name the source, date and local timezone; use America/New_York where that is the source clock, not fixed EST throughout the year.

Neither interval must produce the day’s absolute extreme. A later retracement need not equal 20% or 38.2% of the range. Select the reference and response condition before replay, and keep days with no reversal in the sample.
